data.name: Endpoint Liveness Probe - is this API actually alive?
data.description:
Given any public HTTP(S) URL, returns a measured verdict - LIVE, PAUSED, GATED, CHALLENGED, DEGRADED, DEAD or UNKNOWN - with every reason carrying the source it was read from.

The point is the case a status check misses: a front door answering 200 over a back end that stopped. The probe reads the origin's own machine-readable surfaces (/health, /healthz, /status) alongside the URL you named, flags self-reported paused/degraded states, and flags heartbeat fields that have stopped moving.

If the URL answers HTTP 402, the x402 payment requirements are parsed and returned - price, asset, network and payTo - so an agent learns the price from the endpoint rather than from its seller.

The same endpoint sells deeper units on their own paths, priced per call in the OpenAPI document above: a full-surface due-diligence report on an origin, and a batch probe of up to 50 URLs in one call. Fund a token for the most expensive route you intend to call - the minimum token amount on this listing covers all of them.

Honest-actor rules, enforced in code: the User-Agent identifies the probe truthfully and never impersonates a browser, and robots.txt is read and reported. Nothing here is advice, a signal, or a recommendation to buy or sell anything - the service reports HTTP facts about a URL.

data.name: JP-Structural Margin Oracle
data.description:
JP-Structural Margin Oracle provides AI agents with ready-to-use price anomaly and price-gouging intelligence for the Japanese market.

It analyzes Japanese consumer prices against CPI, currency effects, and underlying cost factors to identify unusual price movements.

Key signals:
• Delta — price growth vs. the CPI baseline
• FX-Adjusted Delta — isolates movements beyond yen depreciation
• SJ-Score — measures price deviation from cost-justified levels

/analyze returns item-level signals, confidence, reason codes, alert levels, and a combined CONFIRMED/POSSIBLE/FAIR verdict.

Updated every 12 hours from official government and multi-source data.

$0.30 USDC per request.

data.name: Sum of Today's date in UTC
data.description:
This service provides a simple mathematical function (summing the digits of today's date)

- Get today's date in UTC (e.g., 2024-06-08).
- Format it as a string: "2024-06-08".
- Split into digits: [2, 0, 2, 4, 0, 6, 0, 8].
- Sum the digits: 2+0+2+4+0+6+0+8 = 22.
- Return a string: "The sum of the digits in today's date is: 22".
